chapter_seo_title: Li Huowang Discovers Retroactive History — Daoguixian Chapter 611
chapter_meta_description: Li Huowang uncovers the horrifying truth: the past itself can be rewritten by the Heavenly Laws. Everyone has forgotten the jade pendant. Was Zhuge Yuan's sacrifice a lie?
og_title: The Jade Pendant — A Reality-Testing Chapter in Daoguixian
og_description: In his investigation of a forgotten jade pendant, Li Huowang proves that the entire history of the Dao-Twisted World can be deleted and rewritten. A milestone of ontological horror.
twitter_title: The past isn't fixed. It's been edited. Li Huowang finds proof.
twitter_description: Li Huowang confirms his worst fear: the True-and-False Heavenly Law doesn't just lie—it rewrites history. This changes everything.

lore_anchors.definition: The authority over the ontological status of events and objects. The possessor can retroactively declare things "false" (non-existent) or "true" (fixed in reality).
A periodic disaster tied to the takeover or shifting of Heavenly Laws, which can cause massive, retroactive changes to history and memory.
The imperial bureau overseeing celestial/supernatural matters, including almanacs and astrology. In this novel, its authority hints at control over recorded time itself.
An intelligence-gathering sect or network to which the informant Liu Zongyuan belongs.
A sect based on pain-worship and self-mutilation. Li Huowang is loosely associated with them.
The sword that connects Li Huowang to the Great Qi realm, currently embedded with the shrunken head of Zhuge Yuan.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why doesn't anyone remember the jade pendant?
cultural_notes_faq.a: Because the True-and-False Heavenly Law changed the historical event that caused the pendant to exist. When the cause was erased, so was the object and everyone's memory of it.
It's the idea that past events are not fixed but can be rewritten by a change in the Heavenly Laws, leaving only a witness (Li Huowang) with conflicting memories.

cultural_notes_faq.q: How does this affect Zhuge Yuan's sacrifice?
cultural_notes_faq.a: Li Huowang now fears the Great Qi that Zhuge Yuan died to save might have been a "deleted" or overwritten timeline—making his heroic sacrifice meaningless.
